name: INS Agray
variant: ASW Corvette / Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC)

header.one_liner: Lead ship of the ASW-SWC (Arnala-class) shallow-water ASW corvette series; first-in-class commissioned 2024, sisters completing at GRSE and (for Agray batch) at Goa Shipyard; hull-integrated sonar; low-visibility ASW specialist for littorals.
header.maker: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE), Kolkata (design + lead series) and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) — the Agray-variant batch
header.indigenous_label: ~80% indigenous by value (GRSE claim); sonar/AA weapons partially imported

what_it_is.prose: Note: 'INS Agray' is used here as the platform entry for the ASW-SWC shallow-water anti-submarine warfare corvette series built under Project P-28I or its commercial-derivative ASW-SWC programme for the Indian Navy. The class — sometimes referred to as the Arnala class — was designed by Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) to counter submarines and undersea threats in India's shallow coastal waters, where large frigates are less effective. The ships carry a hull-mounted sonar and an integrated ASW suite including torpedo tubes, ASW rockets, and a variable-depth sonar variant on later ships, supported by a 30mm/76mm gun for self-defence. The programme is a flagship of the Indian Navy's 'Make in India' littoral ASW build-out, split between GRSE (the original class of 4) and a follow-on tranche (the ASW-SWC 8-ship order of which several hulls are built at Goa Shipyard Limited). As a member of the ASW-SWC programme, the Agray ships are optimised for the shallow-water ASW role, filling a critical gap in India's littoral anti-submarine coverage. The lead-in-series commissioning occurred in 2024; later hulls in the batch commissioned through 2025-2026. 'INS Agray' should not be confused with the earlier, unrelated naval usage of the name; the platform entry here tracks the contemporary ASW-SWC/series programme.

deployments_procurement.summary: The ASW-SWC procurement runs in two tranches: an initial GRSE-designed and built batch (4 ships, ~₹1,571 crore each nominal programme-wide estimate varies) and a larger 8-ship shallow-water craft order placed in 2019 under Project ASW-SWC, split across GRSE (further hulls) and GSL. The Agray series hulls form part of this second, larger programme. Costs are not uniformly published; the class is broadly reported at around ₹1,500-1,600 crore per ship but precise values differ by yard and tranche — flagged as uncertain. The lead ship commissioned in 2024, with sisters following through 2025-26.

faq.question: What does ASW-SWC stand for?
faq.answer: ASW-SWC stands for Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft — a class of coastal anti-submarine corvettes designed by GRSE to operate in India's shallow littoral waters where large frigates are ineffective against submarines and undersea threats.

faq.question: Which shipyards build the ASW-SWC series?
faq.answer: The ASW-SWC programme is split between Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE), which designed the class and built the lead ships, and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL), which builds a tranche of the follow-on hulls.

faq.question: Why does India need specialist shallow-water ASW craft?
faq.answer: Large frigates and destroyers are too big and too deep-draft to effectively hunt submarines in India's shallow coastal waters and straits. Specially designed shallow-water ASW corvettes with hull-mounted sonar fill this littoral coverage gap, protecting ports, sea lanes and the seabed around India's coastline from submarine incursions.
